clue.text: In Paris I work on a ruddy odd quiz show

indicators.note: odd here means the odd-numbered positions, so only the first, third and fifth letters of the word are kept

blocks.note: je is French for I
op is short for opus, a work
taken as written
letters 1, 3 and 5 of ruddy

explanation.surface: Someone in Paris boasts of working on a strange, flushed-faced television quiz programme.
explanation.walkthrough: JEOPARDY! is the long-running American TV quiz show where contestants phrase answers as questions.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeopardy! is a famous example of a television quiz programme, so the general term covers it.

clue.text: Fancy Welshman?

blocks.note: W is the standard abbreviation for Welsh
him refers to a man

explanation.walkthrough: Welshman reads as one word, but it splits into Welsh and man; the question mark warns of the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy, as a noun, is a sudden impulsive desire or notion, the same as a passing caprice.

clue.text: Home country's far from the sea

blocks.note: being in means being at home
a land is a country

explanation.surface: A statement that someone's native country is landlocked, nowhere near the coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Inland describes a place situated in the interior of a region, away from any coastline.

clue.text: Longing to get rid of cap on Sunday pay

indicators.note: the cap of a word is its top or first letter, and getting rid of it drops that letter

blocks.note: a yearning is a longing
S is the abbreviation for Sunday

explanation.surface: A wish to stop wearing a hat when collecting a Sunday wage packet.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the leading Y from the word for longing, then add the Sunday abbreviation at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnings are the money received for work, which is what pay means as a noun.

clue.text: Accidentally conspire, keeping quiet, with suppression of information

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside, so one piece is held within the other
something done accidentally is done haphazardly, so the letters come out in a random order

blocks.note: taken as written
sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: Plotters accidentally end up hushing things up, linked to keeping information from the public.
explanation.walkthrough: The hush sound goes in with the eight letters of conspire, and all ten are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Censorship is the official banning or suppressing of books, news or other information.

clue.text: Stop soldier taking against English at university

blocks.note: a GI is an American soldier
v is short for versus, against
E is the abbreviation for English
a student at university is said to be up, in British usage

explanation.surface: A soldier is halted for siding against the English while studying.
explanation.walkthrough: Being up means being in residence at a university, as in going up to Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: To give up is to stop doing something, a phrasal verb meaning quit.

clue.text: Engineer in charge pursues blokes drinking tea

indicators.note: drinking takes something in, so one word swallows another
to pursue is to follow behind, so the first piece goes after the second

blocks.note: blokes are men
cha is a slang word for tea
IC is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: The engineer in charge follows a group of men having their tea break.
explanation.walkthrough: The tea word sits inside the blokes, and the in-charge abbreviation is placed after them.
explanation.definitionFit: A mechanic is a skilled worker who repairs machines, a kind of engineer in everyday speech.

clue.text: Visit setter in horse yard

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other, which surrounds it

blocks.note: a cob is a sturdy short-legged horse
the setter refers to themself as me
Y is the abbreviation for yard

explanation.surface: An invitation to drop in on the crossword setter, who is with a horse in the yard.
explanation.definitionFit: To come by is an informal phrasal verb for making a short visit to someone.

clue.text: She's a foremost essayist

blocks.note: taken as written
read as fore-most: the front of the word most
Elia was the pen name of the English essayist Charles Lamb

explanation.surface: Praise for a woman as a leading writer of essays.
explanation.walkthrough: Foremost has to be split into fore and most. ELIA, Charles Lamb's pen name, is a crossword favourite for essayist.
explanation.definitionFit: Amelia is a girl's name, so she is a fair stand-in for any female person with that name.

clue.text: Charts turnover of unsolicited emails

indicators.note: a turnover flips something round, so the word is read from the other end

blocks.note: maps are charts

explanation.surface: A graph showing the amount of junk email in circulation.
explanation.definitionFit: Spam is the collective name for unwanted bulk messages sent to many inboxes.

clue.text: Make arrangements for priest after today

indicators.note: after means the first piece is written following the second

blocks.note: AD, anno Domini, labels the present era of years
a minister is a member of the clergy

explanation.surface: Organising things for a clergyman once the day's business is over.
explanation.walkthrough: Today is AD because we are living in the years anno Domini, the era after Christ.
explanation.definitionFit: To administer something is to manage and organise it, making the arrangements for it to run.

clue.text: Took issue with guard about hiding key

indicators.note: about suggests letters moved around, so the word is rearranged
hiding something keeps it tucked inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: taken as written
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: Someone quarrelled with a security guard who was concealing a key.
explanation.definitionFit: To take issue is to disagree or dispute, which is what arguing means.

clue.text: United Nations voting model's within due process and corruption-free

indicators.note: to process something is to work it over, so the letters are rearranged
within places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: UN is the abbreviation for United Nations
a poll is a vote
taken as written
the Model T was Ford's famous car

explanation.surface: A UN-supervised election follows due process and is free of corruption.
explanation.walkthrough: Due process looks like the legal phrase, but process works on due alone; the model letter then sits after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Unpolluted means clean and untainted, and something free of corruption is likewise untainted.

clue.text: Papa's stuck in routine after fund's lost all his money

definitions.note: a verb phrase, read as 'has lost all his money', for an adjective

indicators.note: stuck in means lodged inside, so one piece goes within the other
after means the first piece follows the second

blocks.note: a bank is a fund or store of money
a rut is a dull routine
Papa is P in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Father is trapped in a dull existence after his investment fund has gone under.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone bankrupt is legally insolvent, having no money left to pay what they owe.

clue.text: Yep, pie's cooked — hurray!

indicators.note: cooked means prepared or doctored, so the letters are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cheerful cry that the pie has finished baking.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of delight or celebration, interchangeable as cheers.

clue.text: Issues over group with a title

indicators.note: over in a down clue means turned upside down, so the whole string runs backwards

blocks.note: a set is a group
taken as written
a title is a name

explanation.surface: Problems arising from a group gaining a title.
explanation.walkthrough: Issues looks like a noun, problems, but it is a verb: flows out.
explanation.definitionFit: To emanate is to issue or flow out from a source.

clue.text: Condition a mother to accept son having time with husband

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it in, so the outer word holds the others

blocks.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for son
T is the abbreviation for time
H is the abbreviation for husband
ma is mother

explanation.surface: A family situation in which a mother takes in her son along with her husband.
explanation.definitionFit: Asthma is a medical condition, a chronic disease affecting the airways.

clue.text: Fish tanks losing large number is one of the signs of winter

definitions.text: one of the signs of winter

indicators.note: losing something means it is taken away, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: aquariums are tanks for fish
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Empty fish tanks are a telltale sign that winter has arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: Signs reads as indications, but means signs of the zodiac. Aquarius covers late January to mid-February.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquarius is the zodiac sign for people born from about 20 January to 18 February, in northern winter.

clue.text: Street-ravaged dog takes on energy from pudding

indicators.note: ravaged means wrecked, so the word's letters are scrambled
taking something on means adding it, so the last piece is attached at the end

blocks.note: St is the abbreviation for street
taken as written
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A stray dog on a ruined street gets its strength from a pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: Stodge is heavy, filling food, especially a thick pudding such as a steamed sponge.

clue.text: Beginning to grasp wife in Los Angeles is faithful

indicators.note: grasping something holds it inside, so one piece surrounds another
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: a start is a beginning
LA is the abbreviation for Los Angeles
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: The first step in holding on to a spouse in LA is loyalty.
explanation.walkthrough: The wife letter goes inside LA, and that pair goes inside the beginning word after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalwart supporter is loyal and dependable, the same as faithful.

clue.text: Laugh at Penny leaving tent after drug's brought in

indicators.note: something leaving goes away, so that letter is taken out
brought in means put inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a tepee is a conical tent
P is the abbreviation for penny
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: Mocking a woman named Penny who left a tent after drugs were smuggled in.
explanation.walkthrough: Penny looks like a woman's name but it is the coin. Take its letter out of the tent, then put the drug letter into the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Tee-hee is a giggle or titter, a word for a laugh that imitates the sound.

clue.text: Very old city has a river enshrouded in mist

indicators.note: something enshrouded is wrapped up inside, so it goes within the other piece

blocks.note: V is the abbreviation for very
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia
taken as written
the Po is the main river of Italy

explanation.surface: An ancient city with its river hidden in fog.
explanation.walkthrough: The very letter and the old city join first, and the a-plus-river pair sits between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Mist is fine water vapour hanging in the air, so the broader term covers it.

clue.text: Carry out investigation about oil extract from flower

indicators.note: an extract is something processed out of raw material, so the letters are reworked
about means around, so one piece surrounds the other

blocks.note: to vet is to examine or check carefully
taken as written

explanation.surface: Researching the essential oil drawn from a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: Oil extract looks like perfumery, but extract is the signal to rearrange the oil letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The violet is a small purple-flowered plant, an example of a flower.

clue.text: Ganged up to repair drive

indicators.note: repairing something means putting its parts back together in working order, so the letters are rebuilt

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written; the same word also opens the signal phrase

explanation.surface: People banded together to fix a driveway, or a car's drive.
explanation.definitionFit: Get-up-and-go is energy and enthusiasm, the same as drive in the sense of motivation.

clue.text: Writer O'Brien is wild without measure

indicators.note: without means lacking, so those letters are taken away
wild means out of control, so the letters are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: the name without its apostrophe
an en is a printer's measure of width

explanation.surface: A novelist named O'Brien is going wild beyond all measure.
explanation.walkthrough: Writer suggests an author, given O'Brien, but it is a ballpoint pen. A biro is the British word for a ballpoint.
explanation.definitionFit: A biro is a ballpoint pen, and a pen is a thing that writes.

clue.text: I quit bad habit in Somerset

definitions.note: a prepositional phrase standing for a place in Somerset

indicators.note: quit means leave, so the single letter named goes out of the word
bad suggests something spoiled, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone gave up a bad habit while living in Somerset.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath is a Georgian spa city in the English county of Somerset.
explanation.definitionFit: The city of Bath lies in Somerset, so the phrase points to a place found there.

clue.text: Bishop's jurisdiction keeps soldiers' quarter peaceful

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the outer word surrounds the others

blocks.note: a see is the area a bishop governs
RE, the Royal Engineers, is a British Army corps
N, north, is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: A diocese gives troops a quarter of the city where they can rest in peace.
explanation.definitionFit: Serene describes a calm, untroubled state, the same as peaceful.

clue.text: Returning full-time university student's after flat with lots going on

indicators.note: returning means coming back the way it went, so that abbreviation runs backwards
after means the first pieces follow the last one

blocks.note: flat means even, level
FT is the abbreviation for full-time
U is the abbreviation for university
L, the learner plate, stands for a student

explanation.surface: A student back at university full-time moves into a flat with a busy social life.
explanation.walkthrough: Flat looks like a home, but it means level. L is a learner, from the L-plates on British learner drivers' cars.
explanation.definitionFit: An eventful period is one full of incidents and happenings, so lots is going on.
